text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-euc1-b NLB target-group health check failing in AZ-b — 502/connection_reset spike detected, 30% error rate over 2m. Pager duty: @priya oncall.
priya: seeing a big spike in 502s from gateway -> envoy in AZ-b. metrics: envoy upstream reset, NLB target unhealthy flapping.
toby: confirming, CloudWatch shows target registration unhealthy in AZ-b, 5xxs start ~ 14:03 UTC. other AZs look OK.
elena: any config churn? did we push a new envoy config or node pool?
priya: no pushes in last hour. autoscaling launched a few new envoy pods in AZ-b at 14:01 but they join then deregister.
priya: adding logs snippet: ```
[14:04:12] envoy upstream reset id=0x7f3 error=connection_reset
[14:04:13] http response 502 from upstream target ip=10.0.45.12:8080
[14:04:15] target-health-check FAILED for target id t-xyz status=503
```
ops-bot: Runbook link: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/nlb-target-flap (recommended mitigations: drain AZ, adjust route).
mike-support: Customers reporting latency and error increases for chat endpoints in EU-C. Support queue getting P1 msgs.
priya: quick mitigation plan: (1) mark AZ-b targets unhealthy / drain traffic from AZ-b at NLB level, (2) increase capacity in AZ-a/c, (3) scale envoy warm pools in healthy AZs, (4) monitor for Route53 failover side-effects.
toby: I can do a targeted deregistration of target-group members in AZ-b to force traffic away. doing `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg --targets Id=...` — will do in 60s.
elena: while you do that, I'm going to suspend Route53 health check failover so DNS doesn't oscillate. command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://suppress-failover.json` (prep in progress).
priya: PagerDuty -> update page with mitigation steps and ETA 15m.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by priya. Escalation level: SEV2.
priya: deregister started. running `deregister targets` now.
oby: (typo)
priya: deregister results: 12 targets removed from AZ-b TG, requests redistributed. backend error rate dropping to 8% -> 3m in.
mike-support: ramp down in incoming P1s, sending a customer note: "We are mitigating an infrastructure disruption in EU-C; traffic is being routed away from an affected availability zone. We will follow up with full RCA."
toby: Route53 suppression applied. No DNS churn expected.
elena: also hitting the console to roll back the envoy config on the few new pods in AZ-b to the prior image (they looked suspicious). issuing `kubectl rollout undo deploy/gateway -n prod --to-revision=23` for the AZ-b node selector.
priya: good catch — image 23 -> 22 rolled back. restart observed and pods rejoin healthy but we want them out of rotation for now.
ops-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff in 25m (shift change).
priya: @toby can you take first responder if this persists after I hand off? I'll document runbook steps in the incident thread.
toby: yes I can, happy to take handoff.
pagerduty: Handoff recorded: from priya -> toby at 14:28 UTC.
priya: customer impact summary (so far): ~8% increase in 502s for EU-C chat and embeddings endpoints between 14:03-14:10; affected subset of traffic routed to AZ-b. No data loss, partial request failures and latency spikes. Estimated affected customers: ~12 accounts with elevated errors, 3 reported via support.
mike-support: adding outreach list: payg-corp1, devtools-inc, partner-x. templates sent.
elena: monitoring: 502 rate down to 1.2% overall, envoy resets reduced. Continuing to watch 5m windows.
priya: next steps: keep AZ-b targets out of rotation for 30m, run health-checks, test canary re-add one host after manual verification, follow with full RCA.
toby: noted. I'll keep the channel updated if anything flips.
priya: raising postmortem ticket: https://tracker/redwood/INC-4521 - assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
ops-bot: Auto-note: Incident duration so far 00:25:20.
priya: thanks everyone — handing off to @toby for monitoring and RCA follow-up. :thumbsup:
toby: taking over. will escalate if error rate >5% again.
